title: 从…来看, 拿…来说 and 在…看来: judging from, for example, in one's view
explain: 从 … 来看 'judging from …' gives the basis for a judgement. Put what you look at between 从 and 来看: 从天气来看，明天会下雨 'Judging from the weather, it will rain tomorrow'; 从他的成绩来看，他学得很好 'Judging from his results, he is studying well'.

拿 … 来说 'take … for example, as for …' picks one case to show a general point: 拿我来说，我每天都跑步 'Take me, for example: I run every day'. The case after 拿 is a person or a thing, and the main sentence says something about it.

在 … 看来 'in … view, as … sees it' gives an opinion. What follows 在 is a person or a group: 在我看来，这个计划太难了 'In my view, this plan is too hard'. 在 … 看来 is a person's opinion; 从 … 来看 is about the evidence you look at.

examples.zh: 从天气来看，明天会下雨。
examples.en: Judging from the weather, it will rain tomorrow.

examples.zh: 从他的成绩来看，他学得很好。
examples.en: Judging from his results, he is studying well.

examples.zh: 拿我来说，我每天都跑步。
examples.en: Take me, for example: I run every day.

examples.zh: 在我看来，这个计划太难了。
examples.en: In my view, this plan is too hard.

mistakes: 来看 closes the 从 phrase: 从天气来看 is right; 从来看天气 is wrong.
在 … 看来 needs a person or a group: 在老师看来 'in the teacher's view'. Do not put a thing there: 在天气看来 is wrong.

q.zh: 从天气来看，明天会下雨。
q.en: Judging from the weather, it will rain tomorrow.
q.explain: 从 + evidence + 来看.

q.zh: 拿我来说，我每天都跑步。
q.en: Take me, for example: I run every day.
q.explain: 拿 + example + 来说.

q.zh: 在我看来，这个计划太难了。
q.en: In my view, this plan is too hard.
q.explain: 在 + person + 看来 = in someone's view.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Judging from his results, he is studying well?
options: 从他的成绩来看，他学得很好。
从来看他的成绩，他学得很好。
q.zh: 从他的成绩来看，他学得很好。
q.en: Judging from his results, he is studying well.
q.explain: 来看 comes after the evidence.

q.zh: 在老师看来，这个办法很好。
q.en: In the teacher's view, this method is good.
q.wrong: 在老师的看来，这个办法很好。
q.explain: Do not put 的 inside 在 … 看来.

title: 由此, 总之 and 到…为止: from this, in short, up to
explain: 由此 'from this, hence' leads to a conclusion drawn from what was just said, mostly in writing. 由此可见 'from this it can be seen' is the usual set phrase: 他每天学习五个小时，由此可见，他很努力 'He studies five hours a day; from this it can be seen that he works hard'. 总之 'in short, anyway' sums up several points and starts the closing sentence: 总之，我们要努力学习 'In short, we must study hard'.

到 … 为止 'up to …, until …' marks an end point. The thing after 到 is a time or a stage: 到今天为止，我已经学了一百个词 'Up to today, I have learned one hundred words'; 活动到下周五为止 'The event runs until next Friday'. 为 is read wéi here.

examples.zh: 他每天学习五个小时，由此可见，他很努力。
examples.en: He studies five hours a day; from this it can be seen that he works hard.
In short, we must study hard.

examples.zh: 到今天为止，我已经学了一百个词。
examples.en: Up to today, I have learned one hundred words.
The event runs until next Friday.

mistakes: 由此 and 总之 are more written than 所以. In a casual chat, 所以 sounds more natural.
为止 only goes with 到: say 到今天为止, not 从今天为止.

q.en: In short, we must study hard.
q.explain: 总之 starts the closing sentence.

q.en: The event runs until next Friday.
q.explain: 到 + time + 为止.

q.zh: 到今天为止，我已经学了一百个词。
q.en: Up to today, I have learned one hundred words.
q.explain: 到 … 为止 = up to ….

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He studies five hours a day; from this it can be seen that he works hard?
options: 他每天学习五个小时，由此可见，他很努力。
他每天学习五个小时，由此看他，很努力。
q.zh: 他每天学习五个小时，由此可见，他很努力。
q.en: He studies five hours a day; from this it can be seen that he works hard.
q.explain: 由此可见 is the set phrase.

q.en: In short, we must study hard.
q.wrong: 所以总之，我们要努力学习。
q.explain: 总之 already sums up; do not add 所以.

title: 凭, 依据 and 靠 / 依靠: relying on
explain: 凭 'on the strength of, by' + noun says what makes something possible: 他凭努力考上了大学 'He got into university by working hard'. 凭借 is the formal form: 他凭借自己的经验解决了问题 'He solved the problem by means of his own experience'. 凭什么 asks 'on what grounds?' and sounds sharp: 你凭什么这样说？ 'What gives you the right to say this?'

依据 'on the basis of' + noun is written: 依据这个规定，大家都要早点来 'According to this rule, everyone must come early'. 依据 is also a noun, 'basis': 这个办法没有依据 'This method has no basis'. 根据 (HSK 3) is the everyday word.

靠 and 依靠 'rely on, depend on' say whom or what one depends on: 他靠写文章生活 'He lives by writing articles'; 孩子需要依靠父母 'Children need to rely on their parents'. 靠 also means 'to lean on': 靠在墙上 'lean on the wall'.

examples.en: He got into university by working hard.

examples.zh: 他凭借自己的经验解决了问题。
examples.en: He solved the problem by means of his own experience.

examples.zh: 依据这个规定，大家都要早点来。
examples.en: According to this rule, everyone must come early.
He lives by writing articles.

mistakes: 凭 goes before the verb, with what it rests on right after it: 他凭努力考上了大学. 他考上了大学凭努力 is wrong.
凭什么 is a sharp 'on what grounds?'. For a polite question, use 为什么.

q.en: He got into university by working hard.
q.explain: 凭 + what it rests on + verb.

q.en: He lives by writing articles.
q.explain: 靠 + what one depends on.

q.zh: 依据这个规定，大家都要早点来。
q.en: According to this rule, everyone must come early.
q.explain: 依据 + rule = on the basis of.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Children need to rely on their parents?
q.en: Children need to rely on their parents.
q.explain: 依靠 + the one relied on.

q.en: He got into university by working hard.
q.wrong: 他凭是努力考上了大学。
q.explain: Do not put 是 after 凭.

title: 将, 由 and 所…的: formal 把, by, what someone …
explain: 将 is a formal 把 in writing: 请将书放在桌子上 'Please put the book on the table'; 他将这件事告诉了大家 'He told everyone about this'. The pattern is the same as 把: 将 + thing + verb + something extra after the verb.

由 'by, up to' tells who is responsible: 这件事由他来做 'He will take care of this'; 由你决定 'It is up to you'. It also names who does a job in a formal sentence: 这次会议由经理主持 'This meeting is chaired by the manager'.
所 + verb + 的 turns a verb into 'what someone …': 这是我所知道的 'This is what I know'; 他所说的都是真的 'Everything he says is true'. 所 is formal; in speech say 我知道的 or 他说的.

examples.en: Please put the book on the table.
He will take care of this.
This meeting is chaired by the manager.
Everything he says is true.

mistakes: 将 is for writing and formal speech. In daily talk, 把 is more natural: 请把书放在桌子上.
Do not use 由 for transport. Say 坐火车 'go by train', not 由火车.

q.en: Please put the book on the table.
q.explain: 将 + thing + verb + place.

q.en: This meeting is chaired by the manager.
q.explain: 由 + the person in charge.

q.en: Everything he says is true.
q.explain: 所 + verb + 的 = what someone ….

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He will take care of this?
q.en: He will take care of this.
q.explain: 由 comes before the person.

q.en: Please put the book on the table.
q.explain: 将 and 把 do not go together.

title: 令, 使 and 让: make someone feel
explain: 令 + person + feeling means 'make someone feel …', in writing: 这个消息令大家很高兴 'This news makes everyone very happy'; 他的话令我很感动 'His words move me very much'. 使 (HSK 4) works the same way and is formal too: 这个结果使老师很满意 'This result makes the teacher very satisfied'. 让 is the everyday word: 这个消息让我很高兴.

令人 + adjective is a fixed way to say 'it makes people …': 令人吃惊 'surprising', 令人满意 'satisfying', 令人担心 'worrying'. In 令人 the 人 means people in general, so no one is named. With 使 or 让 you can name the person: 这个消息让我很高兴 'This news made me very happy'.

examples.zh: 这个消息令大家很高兴。
examples.en: This news makes everyone very happy.
His words move me very much.
This matter is surprising.

examples.zh: 这个结果使老师很满意。
examples.en: This result makes the teacher very satisfied.

mistakes: 令 is for writing. In speech use 让: 这个消息让我很高兴.
Something must come right after 令, 使 or 让: 人, 我, 大家 and so on. 这个消息令很高兴 is wrong, because nothing follows 令 to say who is happy.

q.zh: 这个消息令大家很高兴。
q.en: This news makes everyone very happy.
q.explain: 令 + person + feeling.

q.en: This matter is surprising.
q.explain: 令人 + adjective.

q.zh: 这个结果使老师很满意。
q.en: This result makes the teacher very satisfied.
q.explain: 使 + person + feeling.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: This news makes me very happy?
q.en: This news makes me very happy.
q.explain: The person comes before the feeling.

q.en: His words move me very much.
q.explain: Use only one of 令 and 让.

title: 彼此 and 如此: each other, so
explain: 彼此 'each other, one another' shows that both sides do the same thing to each other: 我们彼此了解 'We understand each other'; 同学们彼此帮助 'The classmates help each other'. It is like 互相 (HSK 4) but more formal. 对方 (HSK 4) points to one person on the other side: 我了解对方 'I understand the other person'.

如此 'so, like this' stands for a degree or way that was just mentioned: 他如此努力，一定会成功 'He works so hard that he will surely succeed'; 事情就是如此 'That is how things are'. 如此 is written; in speech say 这么 or 这样.

examples.en: We understand each other.
The classmates help each other.

examples.zh: 他如此努力，一定会成功。
examples.en: He works so hard that he will surely succeed.
That is how things are.

mistakes: 彼此 already means 'each other', so do not add 互相: 彼此互相帮助 repeats the idea.
如此 is formal. In daily speech say 这么 or 这样: 他这么努力.

q.en: We understand each other.
q.explain: 彼此 + verb.

q.en: That is how things are.
q.explain: 如此 = like this.

q.zh: 他如此努力，一定会成功。
q.en: He works so hard that he will surely succeed.
q.explain: 如此 = so, to such a degree.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The classmates help each other?
q.en: The classmates help each other.
q.explain: 彼此 comes before the verb.

q.en: The classmates help each other.
q.explain: 彼此 already means 'each other'.
